markers.description: Hangzhou is the capital of China's Zhejiang province, known for the UNESCO-listed West Lake, the southern terminus of the Grand Canal, and its Longjing tea hills.
markers.name: Hangzhou

markers.description: Nanjing is a county seat in Zhangzhou, Fujian, and a gateway to the UNESCO-listed Fujian tulou roundhouses.
markers.name: Nanjing

markers.description: Shanghai is China's largest city and a global financial center on the Huangpu River, known for the historic Bund waterfront, the Pudong skyline, and the world's busiest container port.
markers.name: Shanghai

markers.description: Wuhan is the capital of China's Hubei province at the confluence of the Yangtze and Han rivers, known for the Yellow Crane Tower, East Lake, and its major universities.
markers.name: Wuhan

markers.description: Wuxi is a city on the shore of Lake Tai in China's Jiangsu province, known for its Grand Canal waterways, the Lingshan Grand Buddha, and its early industrial heritage.
markers.name: Wuxi
